agents.name: billing_agent
agents.description: Explains billing charges using RAG-based policy retrieval and structured billing facts. Accepts a natural-language query that should embed the customer ID and date range so the agent can parse and retrieve relevant policies.
capabilities: Explain specific billing charges and line items for a customer.
Retrieve and cite relevant billing policy documents via RAG.
Compare customer-claimed amounts against actual invoiced totals.
Generate detailed billing reports and analytics for customers.
Handle billing dispute inquiries by referencing policy rules.

query.description: A natural-language billing question. IMPORTANT: embed the customer ID (e.g. 'customer CUST-1001') and date range (e.g. '2019-07-01 - 2019-07-31' or 'July 2019') directly inside the query text so the agent can parse them. Example: 'Why was customer CUST-1001 charged $150 for July 2019?'

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID. If omitted, the agent will parse it from the query string. Format: CUST-1001

start_date.description: Optional explicit ISO start date, e.g. 2019-07-01T00:00:00. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query string.

end_date.description: Optional explicit ISO end date, e.g. 2019-07-31T23:59:59. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query string.

agents.name: anomaly_detection_agent
agents.description: Detects usage anomalies for the demo households over a requested billing window. For the demo, prefer a natural-language query containing `CUST-1001` or `CUST-1002` and a month with year like `Did customer CUST-1001 have a spike in July 2019?`.
capabilities: Analyze large datasets to identify anomalies and outliers.
Use machine learning algorithms to improve anomaly detection accuracy over time.
Provide real-time alerts and notifications when anomalies are detected.
Integrate with various data sources and monitoring systems.

query.description: A natural-language anomaly question. Include `CUST-1001` or `CUST-1002` and a month with year, for example `Did customer CUST-1001 have a usage spike in July 2019?`

customer_id.description: Optional billing customer ID like CUST-1001. For the demo, supported values are CUST-1001 and CUST-1002.

user_id.description: Optional numeric anomaly user ID, e.g. 5997. This is mainly for direct testing; the demo should usually use customer_id.

start_date.description: Optional ISO format start date optionally with timezone, e.g. 2019-07-01T00:00:00-05:00. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query.

end_date.description: Optional ISO format end date optionally with timezone, e.g. 2019-07-31T23:59:59-05:00. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query.

agents.name: customer_lookup_agent
agents.description: Returns customer account profile, plan details, and billing summary.
capabilities: Look up customer profile and account details for billing and general context
Retrieve current plan, pricing, and discount eligibility.
Summarize billing history for specific accounts.

query.description: Natural-language question about a customer. Include CUST-1001 or CUST-1002.

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID like CUST-1001.

agents.name: conversation_summary_agent
agents.description: Summarize previous conversations and extract key takeaways from the orchestrator.
capabilities: Recap and summarize conversational context
Extract key facts from executed agent pipelines

agents.name: weather_context_agent
agents.description: Provides historical weather context for a billing or anomaly window to help explain whether temperature extremes may have contributed to elevated utility usage.
capabilities: Provide historical weather context for a customer's billing window
Help explain whether extreme heat or cold may have contributed to elevated utility usage
Support billing and anomaly investigations with environmental context

query.description: A natural-language weather context request generated by the orchestrator, such as `Check whether weather may explain high usage for customer CUST-1001 in July 2019.`

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID like CUST-1001. If omitted, the agent will parse it from the query.

start_date.description: Optional ISO start date, e.g. 2019-07-01. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query.

end_date.description: Optional ISO end date, e.g. 2019-07-31. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query.

agents.name: solar_performance_credit_loss_agent
agents.description: Monitors a solar customer's recent production against their historical baseline by time of day and season, adjusts expectations using optional weather context, detects likely underperformance before the customer sees it on a bill or true-up, estimates lost generation and credit value, and identifies weather-related, broad-system, or partial-feed issues when solar2 is available.
capabilities: Monitor rooftop solar production against historical baseline by hour-of-day and season.
Detect material solar underperformance across repeated intervals or days.
Use weather context to distinguish weather-related solar drops from likely system problems.
Compare solar and solar2 feeds to identify possible partial inverter or feed issues.
Estimate lost solar kWh, lost credit value, grid import/export context, and customer-facing early-warning summaries.

query.description: A natural-language solar performance question. Include `CUST-1001` or `CUST-1002` and optionally a month with year or date range. Example: `Check solar underperformance for customer CUST-1001 in October 2019.`

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID like CUST-1001. If omitted, the agent parses it from query.

start_date.description: Optional ISO start date. If omitted, the agent parses dates from query or checks the latest recent_days in the meter data.

end_date.description: Optional ISO end date. If omitted, the agent parses dates from query or uses the latest available meter timestamp.

recent_days.description: When no date range is supplied, how many recent days to evaluate.

lookback_days.description: How many prior days to use for the historical solar baseline before falling back to other history.

underperformance_ratio.description: Observed/expected ratio below which an interval counts as underperforming.

min_underperforming_intervals.description: Minimum repeated intervals before flagging a sustained issue.

min_underperforming_days.description: Minimum underperforming days before flagging a sustained issue.

credit_rate_usd_per_kwh.description: Optional net-metering or credit value per kWh. Defaults to the customer's plan overage rate as a proxy.

weather_context.description: Optional output from weather_context_agent used to adjust expected solar generation.

agents.name: bill_shock_forecast_agent
agents.description: Mid-cycle bill forecaster. ONLY call this agent when the customer is asking about an in-progress or upcoming bill — e.g. 'will my bill be high this month?' or 'I'm worried about my current bill'. Do NOT call this for historical billing questions where an invoice already exists (use billing_agent instead). Projects end-of-cycle kWh and dollar total from partial meter readings, applies the customer's tariff, and flags whether the projection is anomalously high vs. recent invoice history. Pairs naturally downstream with program_enrollment_simulation_agent — pass projected_bill_usd and projected_kwh to simulate relief programs against the forecast.
capabilities: Forecast a customer's end-of-billing-cycle kWh and dollar total from mid-cycle meter readings.
Compare a projected bill against the last N billing cycles to flag bill shock with a z-score severity.
Apply the customer's tariff (base charge, overage rate, estimated taxes and surcharges) to projected usage.
Surface contributing factors (usage above historical average, projected baseline overage) for customer alerts.

query.description: A natural-language bill-forecast question. Include `CUST-1001` or `CUST-1002`, optionally a month with year (e.g. `July 2019`) or an explicit `as of YYYY-MM-DD`. Example: `Will CUST-1002 have bill shock for July 2019 as of 2019-07-15?`

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID like CUST-1001. Demo supports CUST-1001 and CUST-1002.

as_of.description: Optional mid-cycle ISO date representing the forecast 'today'. Defaults to the latest meter reading inside the cycle.

cycle_start.description: Optional cycle start ISO date. Defaults to the first day of the as_of month.

cycle_end.description: Optional cycle end ISO date. Defaults to the last day of the as_of month.

lookback_months.description: How many recent invoices to compare the projection against for shock detection.

agents.name: program_enrollment_simulation_agent
agents.description: Simulates the financial outcome of enrolling a customer in a utility support program (level pay, installment plan, low-income assistance, time-of-use). Does NOT actually enroll; returns a per-program comparison so the orchestrator can decide whether to recommend enrollment. Composes downstream of the bill_shock_forecast_agent: pass `projected_bill_usd` and `projected_kwh` to simulate against a forecast rather than a historical invoice.
capabilities: Simulate enrollment in level pay / budget billing using the customer's invoice history.
Simulate splitting a current or projected bill into an installment plan.
Simulate the effect of a low-income assistance discount on the cycle's energy charges.
Simulate time-of-use rates by repricing 15-min meter readings against peak/off-peak rates.
Recommend the program with the largest positive monthly impact for the customer in this cycle.

query.description: A natural-language program-simulation question. Include `CUST-1001` or `CUST-1002` and optionally a month (e.g. `July 2019`). Example: `Would level pay or budget billing help CUST-1002 for July 2019?`

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID like CUST-1001.

programs.description: Optional subset of programs to simulate. Defaults to all four.

cycle_start.description: Optional ISO start date for the cycle being simulated.

cycle_end.description: Optional ISO end date for the cycle being simulated.

projected_bill_usd.description: Optional projected bill total to simulate against. If omitted, the agent uses the invoice on file for the cycle.

projected_kwh.description: Optional projected total kWh for the cycle. Used by the low-income simulation.

installment_count.description: Number of installments for the installment_plan simulation.

low_income_discount_pct.description: Fractional discount applied to energy charges in the low-income simulation (e.g. 0.25 for 25%).

tou_peak_rate.description: Peak-hour $/kWh used by the time_of_use simulation.

tou_off_peak_rate.description: Off-peak $/kWh used by the time_of_use simulation.

assume_eligible.description: If true, the low-income simulation assumes the customer is eligible. Set false to skip that simulation.

lookback_months.description: How many recent invoices to use for the level-pay average.

agents.name: outage_detection_agent
agents.description: Detects power outages affecting a customer's service area within a billing or anomaly window. Maps customer_id to a service area (zip in the demo) and returns reported outage events, total disruption minutes, severity, and a billing-impact hint that the billing agent can use to evaluate service credits.
capabilities: Detect reported power outages affecting a customer's area for a given date range.
Distinguish neighborhood, regional, and scheduled-maintenance events.
Provide outage timing, duration, and severity to support billing dispute investigations.
Hand off a billing-impact hint when a customer was without power during a billing window.

query.description: A natural-language outage question. Include `CUST-1001` or `CUST-1002` and a month with year, for example `Was there an outage affecting CUST-1002 in July 2019?`

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID like CUST-1001. For the demo, supported values are CUST-1001 and CUST-1002.

start_date.description: Optional ISO start date, e.g. 2019-07-01. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query.

end_date.description: Optional ISO end date, e.g. 2019-07-31. If omitted, the agent parses dates from the query.

min_outage_minutes.description: Minimum overlap (in minutes) between an outage event and the requested window for it to be reported.

agents.name: proactive_outreach_agent
agents.description: SCHEDULED USE ONLY — do NOT call this agent in response to an inbound customer query. This agent runs autonomously on a schedule via `scripts/proactive_outreach_runner.py` to proactively contact customers before they reach out. It requires pre-computed signal payloads from other agents (anomaly, bill_shock, solar, payment_risk, etc.) passed as structured objects — string references will not work. It returns whether to contact the customer, the message body, and the recommended channel, but does not send messages itself.
capabilities: Synthesize multiple detector signals into a single prioritized customer alert.
Apply trigger thresholds (severity, spike count, % above mean) to decide whether outreach is warranted.
Apply per-alert-type frequency caps using caller-provided last-outreach state, with outage events bypassing the cooldown.
Compose a customer-facing email/SMS/in-app message with subject, body, and an optional program-enrollment call to action.

query.description: A natural-language outreach evaluation request, e.g. `Evaluate proactive outreach for CUST-1002`.

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID. Demo supports CUST-1001 and CUST-1002.

signals.description: Pre-computed detector outputs keyed by signal type. Pass directly when invoking from the orchestrator's planner or from the proactive outreach runner.

cycle_start.description: Optional cycle start ISO date for context.

cycle_end.description: Optional cycle end ISO date for context.

bill_shock_threshold_pct.description: Minimum projected-vs-average % above which bill shock triggers outreach.

min_anomaly_spike_count.description: Minimum spike count for an anomaly signal to trigger outreach.

last_outreach_at.description: Map of alert_type → last-sent ISO date, used for the frequency cap. Outage events bypass this cap.

cooldown_days.description: Cooldown window (in days) for non-outage alerts.

today.description: Optional ISO date overriding `today` for testing or back-dated demo runs.

agents.name: payment_risk_hardship_agent
agents.description: ALWAYS call this agent when the customer mentions a shutoff warning, payment difficulty, struggling to pay, late payments, or delinquency. Detects customers heading toward delinquency, classifies them into a risk tier (low / moderate / high / critical) using payment history, current balance, days-past-due, and prior support history, and returns prioritized recommendations such as immediate outreach, payment plan, hardship review, due-date adjustment, or autopay enrollment. Designed to compose with `bill_shock_forecast_agent` (pass `bill_shock_severity` as an upstream signal).
capabilities: Classify a customer's delinquency risk tier from payment history, balance, and days-past-due.
Aggregate on-time / late / partial / missed payment counts over a configurable lookback window.
Apply rule-based escalation for shutoff warnings, severe past-due, and repeat missed payments.
Return prioritized support actions (payment plan, hardship review, due-date adjustment, autopay enrollment, immediate outreach) with rationale and concrete numbers.
Surface contributing risk factors to support customer-service explanations and audit trails.

query.description: A natural-language payment-risk question. Include `CUST-1001` or `CUST-1002`. Example: `Is CUST-1002 at risk of delinquency?`

customer_id.description: Optional explicit customer ID. Demo supports CUST-1001 and CUST-1002.

as_of.description: Optional ISO date to evaluate the account snapshot against. Defaults to today.

lookback_invoices.description: Number of recent invoices to summarize when computing the payment-history pattern.

projected_bill_usd.description: Optional projected next-cycle bill from the bill_shock_forecast_agent.

bill_shock_severity.description: Optional severity tier from the bill_shock_forecast_agent (low/medium/high/critical). When high or critical, can elevate a low-risk customer to moderate.
